title: Save your work and send it to GitHub
summary:
Claude changed some files on your computer. These steps store those changes safely and send a copy to GitHub.

You are finished when the GitHub page shows your change at the top of the list.
source: Instructions Claude gave in this conversation
before: The Claude Code window you were just using, still open

words.meaning: The window where you type instructions for the computer instead of clicking. Claude Code runs inside one.
A saved snapshot of your files, with a short note saying what changed.
Sending your saved snapshots from your computer up to GitHub.

steps.title: Ask Claude what changed
steps.do: Click once inside the Claude Code window, where the blinking line is. Paste the text below and press **Enter**.

paste.text: Show me a plain-English list of every file you changed and why.

steps.why: Before you sign for a parcel you look at what is inside. This is the same check: you see what is about to be saved, so nothing goes in that you did not expect.
steps.expect: A short list of file names, each with a sentence saying what changed.
steps.stuck: If Claude says nothing has changed, there is nothing to save. Stop here and tell Claude what you expected to see.

steps.title: Ask Claude to save a snapshot
steps.do: Paste the text below into the same window and press **Enter**. If Claude asks for permission to run a command, press **Enter** again to allow it.
steps.why: A commit is like taking a photo of your desk before you tidy it. If something goes wrong later, you can put everything back exactly as it was in the photo.
steps.expect: Claude replies with a line that starts with a short code of letters and numbers, followed by a one-line note describing the change.
steps.stuck: If you see red text, do not try again. Copy the red text and send it to Claude with the stuck button below.

steps.title: Send the snapshot to GitHub
steps.do: Paste the text below into the same window and press **Enter**.
steps.why: Right now the snapshot only lives on this computer. Pushing is like putting a copy in a safe-deposit box across town: if this computer breaks, the work is still there.
steps.warning: After this step other people who can see the project on GitHub can see your change. Only continue if the list from step 1 looked right.
steps.expect: Claude says the push worked and names the branch it sent.
steps.stuck: If Claude says you are not signed in to GitHub, press the stuck button and say so. Signing in takes one extra step and Claude will walk you through it.

steps.title: Check it arrived
steps.do: Open [github.com](https://github.com) in your web browser. Click your project's name in the list on the left, then click the word **Commits** near the top right of the file list.
steps.why: This is the tracking page for the parcel you just posted. Seeing it listed proves it arrived, instead of trusting that it did.
steps.expect: Your one-line note from step 2 is the first row in the list, with the words "now" or "1 minute ago" beside it.
